memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Patient presents with chronic urticaria, newly diagnosed dyslipidaemia, and hypothyroidism.
He reports daily itchy wheals lasting <24 h, occasional fatigue, and weight gain. On examination, scattered erythematous wheals on trunk and limbs, BP 128/82, pulse 78, BMI 27.4 kg/m², thyroid not enlarged. Smoking status: never. Plan: start levocetirizine 5 mg OD for urticaria, atorvastatin 10 mg HS for lipids, levothyroxine 50 mcg OD for thyroid, and order CBC with eosinophils, TSH, free T4, fasting lipid profile, liver function tests, and creatine kinase.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
CBC: Hb 14.8 g/dL (13-17), WBC 7.2 x10^9/L (4-10), eosinophils 0.6 x10^9/L (0-0.5) slightly high.
TSH 5.8 mIU/L (0.4-4.5) high; free T4 11.2 pmol/L (12-22) low.
Lipids: LDL 152 mg/dL (<100), HDL 38 mg/dL (>40), triglycerides 210 mg/dL (<150).
LFT: ALT 32 U/L (<40), AST 28 U/L (<40), ALP 78 U/L (40-129), GGT 45 U/L (<51).
CK 190 U/L (30-200) normal.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Patient returns for review of urticaria, dyslipidaemia, and hypothyroidism.
Urticaria improved but mild residual itch; fatigue less; weight stable. Exam shows few scattered wheals, BP 126/80, pulse 76, BMI 27.1. Smoking status: never. Labs: TSH down but still high, lipids improved but LDL still high, eosinophils slightly elevated. Assessment: chronic urticaria partially controlled, dyslipidaemia persistently elevated, hypothyroidism inadequately replaced. Plan: increase levothyroxine to 75 mcg OD, switch antihistamine to cetirizine 10 mg HS for nighttime itch, continue atorvastatin 10 mg HS, repeat labs in 6–8 weeks.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Follow‑up visit for chronic urticaria, dyslipidaemia, and hypothyroidism.
Urticaria: occasional wheals, minimal itch, quality of life good. Dyslipidaemia: LDL still above target, triglycerides modestly high. Hypothyroidism: TSH normal, patient reports improved energy. Exam: few faint wheals, BP 124/78, pulse 75, BMI 27.0. Smoking status: never. Plan: add fenofibrate 145 mg OD to address triglycerides, keep levothyroxine 75 mcg OD, continue cetirizine 10 mg HS, repeat lipids and TSH in 3 months.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Review visit for chronic urticaria, dyslipidaemia, and hypothyroidism.
Urticaria: well controlled, no wheals for past 4 weeks. Dyslipidaemia: LDL 115 mg/dL, HDL 42 mg/dL, triglycerides 130 mg/dL after fenofibrate; mild myalgia reported. Hypothyroidism: stable on levothyroxine 75 mcg OD, TSH 2.8. Exam: skin clear, BP 122/80, pulse 74, BMI 26.8. Smoking status: never. Plan: stop fenofibrate due to myalgia, continue atorvastatin 10 mg HS, keep levothyroxine 75 mcg OD, maintain cetirizine 10 mg HS, repeat lipids and LFT in 6 weeks.

Quarterly review for chronic urticaria, dyslipidaemia, and hypothyroidism.
Urticaria: asymptomatic, no wheals. Dyslipidaemia: LDL at goal, triglycerides normal, no muscle symptoms. Hypothyroidism: euthyroid, patient feels well. Exam: skin clear, BP 120/78, pulse 73, BMI 26.5. Smoking status: never. Plan: continue current medications, repeat labs in 4 months, next review in 3 months.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Six‑month follow‑up for chronic urticaria, dyslipidaemia, and hypothyroidism.
Urticaria: remains free of wheals; occasional mild tingling but no lesions. Dyslipidaemia: all lipid parameters within target ranges. Hypothyroidism: stable, TSH 2.3. Exam: skin clear, BP 118/76, pulse 72, BMI 26.2. Smoking status: never. Plan: consider tapering cetirizine to as‑needed basis, continue atorvastatin 10 mg HS and levothyroxine 75 mcg OD, repeat labs in 4 months.
